CHIEF COMPLAINT
Hypogonadism follow-up.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
59-year-old HIV positive male on testosterone replacement therapy presenting for continued care. Patient reports feeling well on current regimen of 1 mL testosterone every 10 days (currently at day 8 of cycle, due to dose Thursday or Friday). He reports improved sense of vigor, better sleep, and improvement in bloodwork since starting testosterone 5 months ago. Patient notes significant improvement in lipid panel with triglycerides decreased from 265 mg/dL to 145 mg/dL and cholesterol improved. Red blood cell count has increased and is stable. Patient currently taking finasteride 5 mg at half-pill dose and cialis; he reports taking 5 mg cialis on workout days and 2.5 mg otherwise, but has been out of cialis. Patient requested increase in testosterone dose from 140 mg to 175 mg. Doctor explained that current testosterone peaks are already greater than 1,500, putting patient at higher risk for blood thickness and cardiovascular complications, and advised against dose increase. Patient also inquired about indole-3-carbinol or broccoli extract for estrogen control. Doctor noted that estradiol levels were previously checked and not elevated, and recommended testing again in the fall if desired but not necessary at this time.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports feeling good overall and sleeping well. Denies concerns.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
HIV positive, hypogonadism.

MEDICATIONS
Testosterone 1 mL every 10 days, finasteride 5 mg half-pill daily, cialis 5 mg on workout days and 2.5 mg other days.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Patient appears trim. Heart and lungs auscultated; sounds good with no concerns.

RESULTS
PSA 0.6 (previously 0.5 last year). Triglycerides 145 mg/dL (previously 265 mg/dL). Red blood cell count increased and stable. Estradiol not elevated.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Patient tolerating testosterone replacement therapy well with good clinical response and improved lipid profile. Advised to continue current testosterone dose of 1 mL every 10 days given acceptable levels with peaks over 1,500 carrying increased cardiovascular risk. Discussed risks of dose escalation. Estradiol testing to be considered in fall if patient desires. Refill prescriptions for testosterone, finasteride, and cialis with paper prescriptions per patient request. PSA to be checked yearly.
